newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian charities launch Burundi peace campaign.
newsitem.headline: Italian charities launch Burundi peace campaign.

text.p: Italian charities on Monday launched a campaign to promote peace in Burundi where civil strife over the past three years has killed some 150,000 people.
"It's not right, it's not civil, it's not Christian," Elvio Damoli, director of the Roman Catholic charity Caritas Italia, told a news conference.
His organisation is leading a group of humanitarian organisations and missionaries in an effort to draw public attention to the situation in the central African state.
Damoli said the campaign would also include a day of prayer for Burundi on December 28 and would seek to influence international organisations such as the United Nations to do more to promote peace.
The campaign was launched to coincide with the third anniversary of the assassination of Burundi's first democratically-elected Hutu president, Melchior Ndadaye.

It was this killing which sparked Burundi's ethnic war in which an estimated 150,000 majority Hutus and minority Tutsis have been killed. The country's perilous condition evokes fears of the genocide in neighbouring Rwanda in 1994.
